title: NY State Assembly · District 36
area: Queens: Astoria and Long Island City

context.text: The seat became vacant when Zohran Mamdani (D) resigned after being elected Mayor of New York City. Diana Moreno won a February 3, 2026 special election with 74.1% of the vote over Rana Abdelhamid (Queens For All) and Mary Jobaida (People First Party).

In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for a full term, incumbent Diana Moreno defeated Mary Jobaida and Kevin Coenen, winning 78.3% of the vote. The Republican and Working Families Party primaries were canceled; Edward Lee (R) and Moreno (WFP) each advanced without appearing on a primary ballot.

candidates.name: Diana Moreno
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 36 (since February 2026)

summary.text: Diana Moreno is the incumbent Assembly Member for District 36, elected in a February 2026 special election to succeed Zohran Mamdani after he became mayor, and then elected to a full term in November 2026. She is an immigrant-rights and labor organizer and a member of the New York City Democratic Socialists of America.

background.text: Moreno was born in Ecuador and immigrated to the United States with her family at age 11.
She holds an associate degree from Santa Fe College and a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida.

Before running for office, she worked as deputy director of the immigrant-advocacy group New Immigrant Community Empowerment and as communications director for the New York State Nurses Association, and organized on behalf of migrant farmworkers, undocumented workers, and unionizing faculty and graduate students.
She was endorsed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the New York City Democratic Socialists of America in both her February 2026 special-election campaign and her 2026 re-election campaign.

priorities.text: "I am a Queens mom, immigrant, organizer, and the Assemblymember for Astoria and Long Island City. I ran for office to fight for working families and ensure that everyone, regardless of income or background, has the opportunity to thrive."
Universal No-Cost Childcare: "I am fighting for universal no-cost childcare because no parent should have to choose between raising their children and making ends meet."

Protect Immigrants & Abolish ICE: "I support New York For All, ending cooperation between New York State and ICE, and building a future where immigrant families can live safely and thrive without fear."

Tenant Protections & Affordable Housing: "I am fighting for stronger tenant protections, deeply affordable housing, and an affordability agenda that helps working families stay in the communities they helped build."

positions.summary: Campaigns on enacting universal, no-cost childcare for children from six weeks to five years old, funded by taxing high earners.
positions.quote: Enact Universal Childcare: Work with Mayor Mamdani to tax the rich and fund free childcare for every New Yorker aged six weeks to five years.

positions.summary: Says she will strengthen tenant protections and defend rent stabilization, and supports creating a public Social Housing Development Authority.
positions.quote: Housing is a Human Right: Strengthen tenant protections, defend rent stabilization, and create a Social Housing Development Authority to build and preserve affordable housing with union labor.

positions.summary: Opposes expanded immigration enforcement; supports the New York For All Act to restrict state and local cooperation with ICE.
positions.quote: Defend Immigrants Without Apology: Stand up for our immigrant neighbors under attack from Trump's cruel and racist deportation machine, and pass the New York For All Act to restrict cooperation with ICE.

positions.summary: Supports taxing high earners to fund public childcare and other services.
positions.quote: Work with Mayor Mamdani to tax the rich and fund free childcare for every New Yorker aged six weeks to five years.

record.text: Prime sponsor of A10340-A, which would increase tax rates on unincorporated businesses and corporations in New York City upon adoption of a local law by the City Council. Amended and recommitted to the Ways and Means Committee on 03/23/2026; remains pending.

Sponsor (introduced by Rules on her behalf) of A11289, the "Not on our dime!" act, which would prohibit not-for-profit corporations from providing unauthorized support to Israeli settlement activity and would create a civil penalty and private right of action for violations. Referred to the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee on 05/08/2026; remains pending.

Sponsor (introduced by Rules on her behalf) of A11580, which would increase penalties on gas and electric utilities for failing to file or correct required annual reports with the Public Service Commission. Referred to the Energy Committee on 06/05/2026; remains pending.
Won the February 3, 2026 special election for Assembly District 36 with 74.1% of the vote, succeeding Zohran Mamdani.

summary.text: Edward Lee is the Republican candidate for Assembly District 36. He describes himself as a longtime independent political activist who has organized cross-partisan candidate forums and debates in New York City.

background.text: Lee says he has been a political activist for over 30 years and founded a project (unifiedplatformusa.com) intended to document areas of agreement among candidates across party lines.
He says he has organized what he describes as New York City's only third-party and independent candidate debates.

priorities.text: Lee's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response focuses on government transparency and accountability and on advocacy work regarding individual cases he says involve wrongful conviction and elder abuse; it does not lay out a conventional legislative platform.
